title: Standardized Imaging and Preprocessing Pipeline for Sugarcane Variety Classification
author: Julio Cesar de Lemos

steps.title: Prepare Sugarcane Samples
steps.instruction: Section sugarcane culms into billets of approximately 30 cm length using a sharp, sanitized machete.

substeps.instruction: Perform swift, transverse cuts to minimize tissue damage and fraying.
Exclude leaves to focus exclusively on stem morphological characteristics.

steps.title: Set Up Imaging Environment
steps.instruction: Arrange billets individually on a uniform matte black flat surface for high contrast.

steps.title: Configure Camera Hardware
steps.instruction: Mount a Canon EOS R8 camera on a fixed tripod perpendicular (90 degrees) to the flat surface.

substeps.instruction: Set the distance between the camera's focal plane and the billet base to exactly 56 cm.

steps.title: Configure Lighting
steps.instruction: Establish controlled lighting to minimize specular reflections and provide diffuse light.

substeps.instruction: Position two softboxes at approximately 45-degree angles on either side of the sample.
Use an integrated 5000K LED strip for additional homogeneous side lighting.

steps.title: Acquire Images
steps.instruction: Capture high-resolution images (6000 x 4000 pixels) in JPG format using manual camera settings (fixed ISO, aperture, and shutter speed).

substeps.instruction: Trigger the camera remotely via smartphone.
Monitor via a dedicated video screen to eliminate physical vibrations.

steps.title: Perform Image Grayscale Conversion and Smoothing
steps.instruction: Convert raw images to grayscale and apply a Gaussian blur using a 5x5 kernel to reduce noise.

steps.title: Segment Sugarcane Stalk
steps.instruction: Apply binary thresholding (e.g., threshold value of 150) to generate an initial binary mask separating the stalk from the background.

steps.title: Crop and Mask Images
steps.instruction: Isolate the sugarcane stalk using contour detection and polygonal approximation.

substeps.instruction: Use cv2.findContours on the binary mask and filter noise by enforcing a minimum area threshold of 130,000 pixels.
Select the largest remaining contour and approximate its shape as a polygon using the Douglas-Peucker algorithm (cv2.approxPolyDP) with epsilon set to 0.1% of the arc length.
Create a precise mask from the polygon and apply it to the image using cv2.bitwise_and.
Crop the image to the bounding box.
Add an alpha channel (cv2.COLOR_BGR2BGRA) to render the background transparent.

steps.title: Export Segmented Images
steps.instruction: Export the resulting segmented images as PNG files with transparent backgrounds.

steps.title: Normalize Image Size
steps.instruction: Resize cropped images to 224x224 pixels using interpolation (e.g., OpenCV's INTER_AREA or INTER_LINEAR) for YOLOv8n-cls model input.
